parsed.explanation: State practice documented here targets gender presentation directly: two transgender women received the five-year statutory maximum in 2021 for wearing women's clothing, and appearance-based convictions carry six months to five years. Security forces arbitrarily arrested at least six and detained eleven people from March 2022 over gender nonconformity, beating two in custody; public beatings of gay and trans people are reported as common, police harassment and extortion are recorded, prisons are described as 'hell', an LGBTQ organisation was shut by police raid, and few lawyers take cases. No execution is documented. Outing probability is high via appearance stops and ID checks; severity after discovery is imprisonment. Appeals sometimes succeed (2013 acquittal; 2021 pair released pending appeal). No visitor-specific border or care rule is sourced.

entry_documents.exposure: Failure to carry identification was charged alongside the anti-homosexuality counts in the 2021 case, compounding the substantive charge; document irregularity can escalate a presentation stop into prosecution. No visitor-specific border screening rule is sourced.
entry_documents.interaction: Document check → appearance mismatch → presentation charges; the identification count stacks on top of the presentation offence rather than substituting for it.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Detention for appearance is routine and prolonged: five months pre-trial in 2021; gendarmes beat two detainees in 2022; detainees threatened with coercive medical examinations to 'prove' conduct.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Release pending appeal was granted in 2021; habeas-type relief not documented as reliable.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Stop for presentation → arrest → five-month custody → maximum sentence; police extortion and false allegations documented as an additional lever.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Prison placement of convicted gender-nonconforming detainees in a facility prisoners call 'hell'; no placement protocol by identity documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Conviction on presentation charges feeds directly into harsh, unregulated custody with beatings recorded.

care_services.exposure: Medical examinations were threatened as coercive proof-seeking against detainees; no trans-specific care access for visitors is sourced.
care_services.interaction: Health setting becomes an investigative exposure channel rather than a care channel when identity is discovered.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Penal code Article 347-1 (five years) plus cybercrime Article 83 reaches online contact; the 2020 assessment ranks prosecution of consensual same-sex conduct among the world's most aggressive; officials frame the law as licensing abuse.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2013 appellate acquittal of appearance-only convictions shows stereotypes can be overturned; 2024 presidential-family coming-out produced hope, but no statutory change.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Statute plus appearance-based enforcement means discovery by any official converts presentation itself into a chargeable act.

minors_guardians.exposure: No minor-specific provision is documented; a travelling minor or accompanying parent would fall under the same appearance-based and association-based enforcement pattern, with custody consequences unresolved.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family travelling together faces the same presentation-stop exposure, aggravated by possible association charges; no data on how minors are processed.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Reporting in 2021 describes public beatings of gay and trans people as common; 2022 group attacks on at least eleven victims with security-force complicity; 2010 report records police harassment, extortion and use of false allegations.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State communication council criticised the 2006 outing publication; president appealed for privacy — rhetoric only.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Civilian attackers act with impunity because the statute licenses them; police become perpetrators or extortionists rather than protectors.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Few lawyers take these cases, an LGBTQ organisation was raided shut, and lawyers called the 2021 judgment political with no proof of acts — recourse is thin.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Appeals produced a 2013 acquittal and 2021 pre-trial release; international human-rights organisations report actively.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Working appellate review is undercut by scarce counsel, closed community infrastructure and beatings in custody; appeal outcome in 2021 case unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: routine arrest on presentation with months of pre-trial custody, beatings in detention, courts deferring (the 2021 conviction proceeded with 'no proof of any act'), and remedies largely illusory given few willing lawyers. Lower than 0.15-A only because no capital provision is documented and appeals occasionally succeed; no execution pathway appears anywhere in the record.

Higher than this anchor: 0.25-B features short jail terms, abolished flogging, no realistic execution, and intermittent rather than systematic custody. Here maximum five-year sentences for clothing are actually imposed, plus beatings in custody and an aggressive national prosecution profile — a heavier and more continuous exposure.

Materially lower: 0.45-A's exposure is routine verification, humiliation and occasional detention with prosecutions uncommon and sentences unlikely. Here arrest on appearance alone yields five-year maximum terms, so severity after discovery is imprisonment, not administrative friction — a full tier or more below.

parsed.synthesis: The combined operative regime is state-directed targeting layered on criminalisation. Article 347-1 and the appearance-based charging practice mean a transgender visitor's presentation is itself the offence: discovery by restaurant staff, police or an ID check converts ordinary presence into a five-year-maximum prosecution, with an added identification charge. Custody brings beatings and a prison prisoners call 'hell'; police add extortion and false allegations; civilians attack with legal cover; community infrastructure and defence counsel are depleted. The 2022 arbitary-arrest pattern shows this operates currently, not as a dormant statute. Partial mitigation: no execution documented, appeals sometimes reverse appearance-only convictions, and international organisations report. Those reduce severity slightly but cannot offset imprisonment after discovery.
